verifications.claim: Vaccines stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: mRNA vaccines contain the genetic code of the virus the body can use to create antibodies to fight the virus; Vaccines are used to boost your immune system
verifications.reasoning: R2 describes vaccines boosting the immune system and specifically mentions antibody production for mRNA vaccines, but does not explicitly state this for all vaccines.

verifications.claim: Vaccines stimulate the body’s immune system to create an imitation infection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Vaccines imitate an infection to trigger the body's natural defenses.
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly states that vaccines imitate an infection.

verifications.claim: The imitation infection is a mild form of the actual disease.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: Live virus vaccines use a weakened (attenuated) form of the virus. The measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine and the varicella (chickenpox) vaccine are examples.
verifications.reasoning: R2 describes weakened forms for live vaccines but not for all vaccine types that imitate infection.

verifications.claim: The imitation infection does not cause the disease itself.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: This teaches your body to fight off these germs without the risk of a full-blown infection.
verifications.reasoning: R2 explicitly states no risk of full-blown infection.

verifications.claim: Vaccination teaches the immune system to recognize and fight the pathogen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: This teaches your body to fight off these germs; Your immune system learns to recognize and attack the infection.
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly supports teaching the immune system to recognize and fight.

verifications.claim: Vaccination enables the immune system to combat the real disease upon future exposure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Your immune system learns to recognize and attack the infection if you are exposed to it later in life. As a result, you will not become ill, or you may have a milder infection.
verifications.reasoning: R2 directly describes response to future exposure.

verifications.claim: The body develops T lymphocytes and B lymphocytes that remember how to fight the infection.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference mentions T lymphocytes or B lymphocytes.

verifications.claim: Routine vaccines include Tdap, flu, and MMR.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: COMMON IMMUNIZATIONS: Influenza vaccine, Tdap vaccine, MMR vaccine; All adults need these routine vaccines: Flu vaccine (influenza) Tdap vaccine
verifications.reasoning: R2 lists them as common immunizations; R4 lists flu and Tdap as routine for adults, MMR as childhood.

verifications.claim: Immunization protects against or reduces the severity of influenza, tetanus, measles, polio, and COVID-19.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Influenza (flu) Offers protection against the flu and the more serious complications; tetanus, diphtheria, measles... polio; COVID-19 Helps reduce the risk of severe illness; Vaccines help protect against many diseases that used to be much more common. Examples include tetanus... measles... polio.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm protection or reduced severity for each listed disease.

verifications.claim: Childhood immunizations include DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), Hib, polio, MMR (measles, mumps, rubella), and chickenpox.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: DTaP vaccine (Diphtheria, Tetanus, Pertussis) Hib vaccine MMR vaccine Polio vaccine Chickenpox vaccine; recommends 11 vaccines... diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, Haemophilus influenzae type b... polio, measles, mumps, rubella... chickenpox.
verifications.reasoning: R3 and R2 directly list these as childhood vaccines.

verifications.claim: Adult vaccines include annual flu shot, Tdap, shingles, and RSV.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All adults should get an annual flu shot and stay up-to-date with their Tdap vaccine... Shingles 50+ RSV 75+, 50–74 at increased risk.
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly lists these for adults.

verifications.claim: Common minor side effects of immunizations include fever or soreness.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: mild flu-like symptoms, such as fatigue, muscle aches, and low-grade fever; soreness or swelling; Redness or soreness at the injection site Low-grade fever
verifications.reasoning: R5 and R7 directly mention fever and soreness as minor side effects.

verifications.claim: Immunizations can cause soreness or swelling at the injection site.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: minor soreness or swelling around the injection site; Redness or soreness at the injection site
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by R5 and R7.

verifications.claim: Pharmacies like Walgreens and medical offices offer routine vaccines
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Immunization Services... Walgreens... Flu, COVID-19, RSV, pneumococcal—these are just some of the vaccines our pharmacists can help you stay up-to-date on.
verifications.reasoning: R1 is from Walgreens explicitly offering routine vaccines; medical offices implied in other contexts.
